data.summary: Live, SW-live-smoke box1: launched with --dir on a linked worktree lane-wt (branch lane/smoke-toy), the lane's ddflow_claim answered how=created, here=false and made .ddflow/worktrees/smoke-toy, because the lane's MCP entry pins --repo to the primary. The pre-tool hook is rooted at the launched tree, so the lane's write into the tree claim named was refused as outside the lane worktree, and the commit in lane-wt left the item's branch empty, so the gate record was refused until the lane rebound itself with ddflow_task update worktree. Passing the item's default tree path and branch as Request.worktree avoids it (boxes 2 to 9). A launcher must do that or claim must adopt the lane's tree.

data.summary: endpoint.resolve refuses a route with no verified tool_call, and launch() gives no way to pass require_tools=False, which OC.prepare has. So the first live probe of any route cannot go through launch(): SW-live-smoke had to write tool_call as verified in the sandbox's local catalog BEFORE the evidence existed. A probe route needs its own explicit path, not a false fact.

data.body:
D-swarm-pilot-2026-11-05. Nothing has ever run against a live model. Prove one real lane end to end: claim, edit, commit, heartbeat, gate record, stop at the lease. Provides the ddflow lanes smoke route that opencode.py names (Ba655b17982) and sets tool_call_reliable from evidence. Operator consent to this run is recorded. Adopt what B-ac-smoke plans rather than a second runner.

RESULT 2026-11-05: GO for SW-pilot-toy, with conditions. Stopped by the unwind order D-unwind-for-kilo-2026-11-05: NOT merged. Full evidence: docs/ddflow/research/swarm-smoke.md on branch ddflow/SW-live-smoke, commit 4a5c87000; research R4faa82dbf9.

Evidence: kilo 7.8.18 on two keyless LAN DeepSeek models, 11 throwaway sandbox repos. Claim, edit, commit, heartbeat, gate record and stop worked; a clean run took 30 s. Conformance reached level 6 of 7 in 5 of 5 runs, with sandbox timings. The plugin refused real calls live: a write outside the globs and a write after revocation, and both models then stopped. A shell-written file was refused at commit. Tool calls: 86, 85 well formed (flash 61/1, pro 25/0). The stream matches STREAM_RULES, error shape included. Toy items and short runs only.

How it was driven: a sandbox test harness called launch() directly and stubbed both person approvals in memory only; nothing was written to a log as a person's act. tool_call was asserted verified in the sandbox catalog before the evidence existed (Bc64f9048f5).

Conditions: B7d091d0f35 (a lane must get the item's own tree), B72bcd17b4e (conformance defaults give level 0 on a live lane), B09100a25b3 and B6eaa5f27c2 (level 7 unreachable; refused calls count as success), B8478a28c60 (any agent on a clone can release a peer's lease). Also B59a07c283d, B34e7a7001f (low). Still open from before: B5c8139e564, B8647b69e06, Ba655b17982.

Not delivered: `ddflow lanes smoke` (outside this item's globs, and it is launcher work). No route fact was written: there is no .ddflow/local/models.toml here; smoke.tool_call_fact gives verified true for both routes.

To resume: gates research, rules and implement passed. rubber_duck and critic did not run: one combined review was cut off by my 560 s timeout with no result, so it is neither passed nor failed. Then standards, ci, unit_tests, bug_hunt, dedupe, merge. data.command: [REDACTED:path] -m ddflow --agent=sw-smoke review SW-live-smoke --gate rubber_duck,critic --intent 'Judge a live lane run from its stream and event log; record the first live smoke evidence. Not a runner; no CLI route.'

chunk_findings.detail: `_stop` only detects the end of the lease by scanning call details for exactly `LEASE_GONE` (`"holds no live lease"`). But `_refusal` classifies a heartbeat answer of `{"renewed": false}` as `REFUSED` with detail `"the heartbeat renewed nothing"`, which the function's own docstring says means the lane has no lease to go on with. Concrete input: step 1 `write` OK, step 2 `heartbeat` OK, step 3 `heartbeat` output `{"renewed": false}`, step 4 a non-write call OK, `exit_code=0`, no `past` events. `_heartbeat` passes because of the earlier OK heartbeat; `_stop` finds no `LEASE_GONE` in any detail, so it returns PASSED. The lane made a call after its lease ended, yet the run is judged PASSED.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/lanes/smoke.py:_stop

chunk_findings.detail: `_stop` returns `UNAVAILABLE` for `exit_code is None` before checking the `past` events. Since `past` events are definitive failures (`item.completed` or `worktree.merged`), a run where the lane emitted `item.completed` but its exit was not observed is reported as unavailable rather than failed. If the other checks pass, `Verdict.outcome` becomes `UNAVAILABLE`, so a concrete failure is not counted as a failure in `majority`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/lanes/smoke.py:_stop

chunk_findings.detail: The document states `smoke.judge` reports the Heartbeat step as failed for runs 8 and 9, while also explaining that those runs’ items did not ask for a heartbeat. A guard-test lane that correctly never emits a heartbeat should produce “not applicable” for that step, not “failed”; given the stream/event log for run 8 or 9, the judge will falsely mark a successful lane run as failing the heartbeat step, contaminating the go/no-go evidence.
chunk_findings.title: docs/ddflow/research/swarm-smoke.md:33

chunk_findings.detail: `majority` treats an unavailable run as a vote against passing but not against failing, which breaks its own rule that an unavailable run is no vote for either. Given `["passed", "passed", "unavailable", "unavailable"]`, `passed * 2 > len(outcomes)` is `4 > 4`, `failed` is 0, and the function returns `unavailable` even though the only votes are 2–0 for pass. The mirror input `["failed", "failed", "unavailable", "unavailable"]` returns `failed`. Abstentions therefore block a pass and still let a failure win.
chunk_findings.title: majority

chunk_findings.detail: `_refusal` returns `""` both for “no ddflow refusal” and for a ddflow refusal whose reason is the empty string: `{"refusal": {"reason": ""}}`. `_call` decides refused vs OK by the truthiness of that return, so such a completed call is recorded as `OK`. A write tool with that output is then counted by `_edit` as a file write that went through, and a heartbeat with that output is counted by `_heartbeat` as renewed, letting a refused call contribute to a pass.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/lanes/smoke.py:_refusal / _call

chunk_findings.detail: `_stop` checks `exit_code is None` before checking `past`. If the event log contains `item.completed` or `worktree.merged` under this lane’s identity but the lane’s exit was not observed, it returns `UNAVAILABLE`, not `FAILED`, even though the event evidence already proves the lane went past its brief. That converts a clear failure into “unavailable” and can change the final run outcome.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/lanes/smoke.py:_stop

chunk_findings.detail: This new file is the SW-live-smoke task and announces itself as a task at line 3, but it nowhere names its phase, states its dependencies with `needs`, or carries a `wave:N`/`no-deps` tag. The rule requires every task to name the phase it counts toward, state its dependencies, and carry a wave tag; a task with no prerequisite must still carry `no-deps`. As written, `ddflow waves --stamp` cannot process this task and the absence of `no-deps` leaves the lack of a prerequisite as an omission rather than a decision.
chunk_findings.title: docs/ddflow/research/swarm-smoke.md:1 [r-task-phase-needs-wave]

chunk_findings.detail: The test calls `judged(events=[*log(), ev("item.completed")])` with the default `exit_code=0`. The clean-run test, `test_a_clean_run_passes_every_step`, proves that with `exit_code=0` and no guard refusal the `stop` check is `S.PASSED`; the extra `item.completed` event is precisely the event the test says must be ignored, so the correct result for `stop` is still `S.PASSED`. The assertion `outcomes(v)["stop"] == S.FAILED` is therefore wrong and will fail against a correct `smoke.py`.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_lanes_smoke.py:test_completing_its_own_item_is_not_stopping

chunk_findings.detail: `majority` treats unavailable runs as votes in the pass denominator while its own contract says they are not votes. Given outcomes `[PASSED, PASSED, FAILED, UNAVAILABLE, UNAVAILABLE, UNAVAILABLE, UNAVAILABLE]` (2 pass, 1 fail among votes), `passed * 2 > len(outcomes)` is `4 > 7`, then `failed >= passed` is false, so the function returns `UNAVAILABLE` instead of `PASSED`.
chunk_findings.title: majority

If the other checks pass, `Verdict.outcome` becomes `UNAVAILABLE`, so a concrete failure is not counted as a failure in `majority`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/lanes/smoke.py:_stop

chunk_findings.detail: The document states `smoke.judge` reports the Heartbeat step as failed for runs 8 and 9, while also explaining that those runs’ items did not ask for a heartbeat. A guard-test lane that correctly never emits a heartbeat should produce “not applicable” for that step, not “failed”; given the stream/event log for run 8 or 9, the judge will falsely mark a successful lane run as failing the heartbeat step, contaminating the go/no-go evidence.
chunk_findings.title: docs/ddflow/research/swarm-smoke.md:33

chunk_findings.detail: `majority` treats an unavailable run as a vote against passing but not against failing, which breaks its own rule that an unavailable run is no vote for either. Given `["passed", "passed", "unavailable", "unavailable"]`, `passed * 2 > len(outcomes)` is `4 > 4`, `failed` is 0, and the function returns `unavailable` even though the only votes are 2–0 for pass. The mirror input `["failed", "failed", "unavailable", "unavailable"]` returns `failed`. Abstentions therefore block a pass and still let a failure win.
chunk_findings.title: majority

chunk_findings.detail: `_refusal` returns `""` both for “no ddflow refusal” and for a ddflow refusal whose reason is the empty string: `{"refusal": {"reason": ""}}`. `_call` decides refused vs OK by the truthiness of that return, so such a completed call is recorded as `OK`. A write tool with that output is then counted by `_edit` as a file write that went through, and a heartbeat with that output is counted by `_heartbeat` as renewed, letting a refused call contribute to a pass.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/lanes/smoke.py:_refusal / _call

chunk_findings.detail: `_stop` checks `exit_code is None` before checking `past`. If the event log contains `item.completed` or `worktree.merged` under this lane’s identity but the lane’s exit was not observed, it returns `UNAVAILABLE`, not `FAILED`, even though the event evidence already proves the lane went past its brief. That converts a clear failure into “unavailable” and can change the final run outcome.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/lanes/smoke.py:_stop

chunk_findings.detail: This new file is the SW-live-smoke task and announces itself as a task at line 3, but it nowhere names its phase, states its dependencies with `needs`, or carries a `wave:N`/`no-deps` tag. The rule requires every task to name the phase it counts toward, state its dependencies, and carry a wave tag; a task with no prerequisite must still carry `no-deps`. As written, `ddflow waves --stamp` cannot process this task and the absence of `no-deps` leaves the lack of a prerequisite as an omission rather than a decision.
chunk_findings.title: docs/ddflow/research/swarm-smoke.md:1 [r-task-phase-needs-wave]

chunk_findings.detail: The test calls `judged(events=[*log(), ev("item.completed")])` with the default `exit_code=0`. The clean-run test, `test_a_clean_run_passes_every_step`, proves that with `exit_code=0` and no guard refusal the `stop` check is `S.PASSED`; the extra `item.completed` event is precisely the event the test says must be ignored, so the correct result for `stop` is still `S.PASSED`. The assertion `outcomes(v)["stop"] == S.FAILED` is therefore wrong and will fail against a correct `smoke.py`.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_lanes_smoke.py:test_completing_its_own_item_is_not_stopping

chunk_findings.detail: `majority` treats unavailable runs as votes in the pass denominator while its own contract says they are not votes. Given outcomes `[PASSED, PASSED, FAILED, UNAVAILABLE, UNAVAILABLE, UNAVAILABLE, UNAVAILABLE]` (2 pass, 1 fail among votes), `passed * 2 > len(outcomes)` is `4 > 7`, then `failed >= passed` is false, so the function returns `UNAVAILABLE` instead of `PASSED`.
